sector_model: regional casino operator: net revenue, property EBITDA margin, depreciation roll-off, capex, net cash, buybacks; litigation contingency; nonfinancial FCF
thesis: Monarch Casino & Resort (Atlantis Reno, Black Hawk CO) has no debt, 137.4M cash and 99.4M undrawn revolver at 2026-09-30. Trailing twelve month (TTM) figures built from FY2025 10-K plus nine-month deltas: net revenue 565.4M, net income 115.1M, diluted EPS 6.31, operating cash flow 168.2M, acquisition of property and equipment 25.6M, free cash flow about 142.6M. At the 2026-11-06 close of 108.75 and 17,635,985 shares (cover, 2026-10-28) market cap is about 1.918B: 17.2x TTM EPS, 7.4% FCF yield, about 1.78B enterprise value (market cap less cash, no debt; operating leases only 12.6M). Nine-month EPS rose 21.1% to 5.06 on revenue +5.0%, and buybacks (54.9M in 9M, 300,859 shares for 37M in Q3) plus 16.0M dividends are funded from cash flow.
counterthesis: Most of the profit jump is accounting, not demand: nine-month depreciation fell to 31.9M from 40.8M because the 2020 Black Hawk tower became fully depreciated by Q4 2025 (an 8.9M pre-tax tailwind versus a 16.4M rise in operating income), and Q3 revenue grew only 2.4% with net income +1.4%. Nine-month capex is unusually low (19.6M vs 30.4M) and TTM capex of 25.6M may understate maintenance needs, flattering FCF. A multi-year construction dispute with PCL (a February 2025 judgment that the company disputes; 3.3M of judgment interest accrued in 9M2026; the lender waived default; the Gilpin County stay was lifted effective 2026-09-16) has an outcome the company says it cannot estimate. Regional gaming is cyclical and exposed to consumer spending, and Reno and Black Hawk concentration is high. The stock fell 5.2% in the 11-03 to 11-06 window after the earnings week (114.74 on 11-02 to 108.75).
invalidation: Q4 and Q1 net revenue turning negative year over year; property EBITDA margin falling under about 30% after the depreciation tailwind; maintenance capex rising above about 40M a year; an adverse PCL ruling above about 100M or lender default; buybacks financed with revolver draws.
